records.text:
- Histopathology findings:  
  1. Biopsy from scalp papule showed:  
     - Dense fibrosis with thick collagen bundles throughout dermis  
     - Prominent decrease of hair follicles  
     - Fibroplasia arranged in whorled and onionskin pattern  
     - Capillary vessel proliferation with ectasia between collagen bundles  
     - Scattered fibroblasts  
     - Perifollicular fibrosis with distortion of hair follicles  
  2. Biopsy from facial papule showed:  
     - Features of angiofibroma  
  Images:  
  - Figure A: Clinical photograph showing firm plaque with superimposed papules and decreased hair density  
  - Figure B: Histology showing diffuse dense fibrosis  
  - Figure C: Histology (H&E) showing capillary vessel proliferation with ectasia  
  - Figure D: Histology showing perifollicular fibroblastic proliferation.

records.query: Need the patient's TSC1/TSC2 genetic testing results, as a positive mutation would definitively confirm tuberous sclerosis complex; also need brain MRI and renal ultrasound to evaluate for cortical tubers/subependymal nodules and angiomyolipomas, which are major diagnostic criteria and would consolidate the diagnosis.

bindings.label: A man in his 20s has a 6-year history of multiple growing papules superimposed on an asymptomatic firm plaque on the occipital scalp

At 3 years of age, scarlike macules appeared on the occipital scalp and coalesced to form a larger plaque with sparse hair; simultaneously, multiple brown-red, dome-shaped papules developed on the nose and gradually evolved to involve the cheeks
Rubbery plaques developed on the sacrococcygeal area, along with hypopigmented patches on the right buttock
The lesions were never ulcerated or inflamed, but hemorrhage occurred occasionally after rubbing
Physical examination revealed a group of unevenly distributed skin-colored-to-pink, discrete, coalescing papules superimposed on a firm plaque on the occipital scalp
The patient has no systemic symptoms or mental impairment and denied a family history of genetic disease
Scalp biopsy shows dense dermal fibrosis with whorled/onionskin collagen bundles, perifollicular fibrosis, decreased follicles, and capillary ectasia (hamartomatous collagenoma)
Facial papule histology is consistent with angiofibroma
